# Quote Build

Pricing a make-to-order job means building up a cost and then applying
commercial judgment. Every job is priced fresh, which is why quoting is skilled,
slow, expert work — and why the estimator is usually the bottleneck.

**The cost basis is shown, always.** A quote that says *$14,720* is useless. One
that says *$14,720, of which $6,100 is material at the price we paid on PO-8841
in June, plus 8% scrap* is defensible.

**Quick start**

```
→ Load the intake form. Lines with no quantity or no material are skipped; quote the rest and list what's blocked
→ Find comparables; show what made each one comparable AND how this job differs
→ Flag capability BEFORE pricing. Then hours per op from the ladder: routing → actuals → confirmed design → first principles
→ Setup and run separate at every rung. A superseded routing is shown, never priced. probable_standard never outranks rung 3
→ Build up the cost: material, labor, machine, setup, outside processing, tooling
→ Resolve rates: MFG_* variable, then the plant profile. Never asked in the run, never invented
→ Re-amortize setup at every quantity break
→ Margin on its own line. Never buried
→ Check the promised date against real shop load. Never quote a date blind

I wrote the draft customer quote and the internal cost sheet, but every price in the quote is marked pending. No other skill was chained (`customer-inquiry-intake` did not run, so I built a minimal intake from the RFQ files).

**Why there is no price:**
- **No purchase orders.** The request says they are in `inputs/cost`, but that folder holds only `closed_jobs.csv` and `routings.csv`, and a search of all the inputs found no PO file. With no PO, supplier quote or standard cost, material has nothing to price from.
- **No rates on file.** No `MFG_*` variable is set and no plant profile or rates file exists. Finance's memo is not a recorded rate, so under the skill's rules it was not used and its values are not repeated anywhere. To use it, record it through onboarding ("update our labour rate", plus burden, margin rules and scrap basis) or set the `MFG_*` variables; the quote then completes. The memo gives one fully burdened rate per work centre, while the plugin keeps labour and burden separate, so that mapping needs deciding when it is recorded.
- **No anodize vendor price or lead time** in the inputs.
- **No MB-2040 drawing.** The package is a text spec only, so once priced this can only be a budgetary estimate, never a firm quote.
- **No MB-2040 routing or closed jobs.** Every operation's hours are a stand-in taken from the similar MB-1880 Rev B bracket, the weakest basis in the skill's ranking.

**What I could produce:**
- **Hours per quantity (internal only).** Setup and run are kept separate. Setup is 1.75 h per job, so 0.0070 / 0.0035 / 0.00175 h per piece at 250 / 500 / 1,000.
- **Cross-check against MB-1880 closed jobs.** Op 20 setup on WO-7702 is 15.6% over its routing, above the 15% default threshold (not plant-set).
- **1,000 pcs is an extrapolation.** It is 2.0x the largest closed job, which was for a different part.
- **Date not checked.** There is no planning export, so the 15 Jan 2027 first-article date and the lead time are not confirmed.
- **Bore tolerance and finish not checked** against what the plant has demonstrated, because there is no plant profile.
- **Every number is computed by script** and listed in the figures block (46 rows).
- **Outbound check on the customer block passed.**

**Files written (all under `C:/LMFG/runs/B05-negative/work/`):**
- `out/quote-build_reply_MB-2040.md`: the full draft, with the customer block and the internal cost sheet
- `out/figures-block_MB-2040.csv`
- `out/records/intake_MB-2040_minimal.yaml`
- `out/records/operation-record_MB-2040_revC.yaml`
- `scripts/figures.py`: the script that computes the figures block

**Questions recorded instead of asked:**
- For the customer, written into the quote but not sent: the released Rev C drawing, the mounting-face flatness requirement, where to mark the part number and lot code, and their payment, freight, packaging and liability terms.
- For the estimator: who to record as releasing the quote, and the bid/no-bid decision, which was never confirmed.

**Could not do:**
- **No price, total or lead time**, for the reasons above.
- **No Word or Excel copies.** python-docx and openpyxl are not installed, so the full draft was saved as one `.md` file, which the skill's own file rules don't allow for a document.
- **No sales command-center page**, because nothing was quoted.
- **The skill's step to look for saved plant setup pages was skipped**, because this run does not allow artifact tools.
